page: Microsoft Azure E96-24s_v5 belongs to the memory-optimized ESv5 family, utilizing a constrained vCPU profile built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine runs on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. It is provisioned with 24 dedicated vCPUs derived from 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The cache hierarchy includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 105 MB L3 cache. System memory measures 672.0 GB, providing an exceptionally high ratio of 28.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The hardware exposes AVX-512 vector extensions alongside cryptographic acceleration instructions including AES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark assessments reflect a profile heavily biased toward memory throughput rather than raw aggregate processing power. In memory tests, the instance placed within the top 25 percent for large-block uncached memory write bandwidth at 106.74 GB/sec, corroborated by a strong PassMark memory score of 2894.78. Conversely, general computational scores remain within the middle 50 percent, with Geekbench single-core at 1712.0, multi-core at 12123.0, and PassMark CPU at 30451.25. Synthetic in-memory operations recorded 23.93 million Redis SET operations per second and 12292.13 PassMark database operations, aligning with anticipated performance for its 24-thread compute ceiling.

Architecturally, the server includes no local ephemeral storage and provides zero hardware accelerator GPUs, mandating the use of network-attached block storage for data durability. The primary architectural tradeoff of the E96-24s_v5 is its reduced core-to-memory ratio; it allocates the memory footprint of a 96-vCPU chassis to only 24 active vCPUs. This makes it particularly cost-efficient for commercial database platforms and analytics software licensed on a per-core basis, where massive memory footprints are required without triggering excessive core-based software fees. Appropriate workloads include large-scale Redis or Memcached clusters, enterprise in-memory databases, and memory-intensive ETL transformations.
description: Microsoft Azure E96-24s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configured with a constrained vCPU topology to maximize memory allocation per compute unit. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, the instance delivers 24 dedicated vCPUs across 12 physical cores alongside a massive 672 GB of RAM, equating to 28 GB per vCPU. The underlying architecture features a 105 MB L3 cache and supports AVX-512 vector instruction extensions. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-quartile memory performance, highlighted by 106.74 GB/sec large-block uncached write bandwidth, while general CPU execution metrics sit in the middle tier. The server contains no bundled local disks, relying entirely on network-attached remote storage volumes for persistence, and includes zero onboard GPUs. This configuration offers high cost efficiency for software requiring substantial memory footprints without demanding high per-core licensing overhead, making it well matched for in-memory databases, Redis caches, and heavy analytics pipelines.
